Dhyānabindūpaniṣad
------------------------------------------
This is one of the minor उपनिषद्स् belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda and classed among the योग-उपनिषद्स् or उपनिषद्स् dealing with the several yogic practices. It is in the anuṣṭubh metre the number of verses being 106.
The Upaniṣad starts with an eulogy of योग. Then comes a description of ब्रह्मन् as extremely subtle and also as all-pervading. This is followed by a picturesque depiction of प्रणव or Om, and meditation on it.
Meditation on वासुदेव (who is ब्रह्मन् with attributes) in the lotus of the heart as also its fruit is given next.
Then, the योग of six steps (ṣaḍaṅga-योग) comprising आसन (posture), prāṇā-yāma (breath-control), प्रत्याहार (with-drawal of मिन्द् from sense-objects), धारणा (fixing the मिन्द् on the object of meditation), ध्यान (meditation) and समाधि (superconscious experience) is described.
A delineation of the चक्रस् like mūlā-dhāra and the कुण्डलिनी power follows next. The five major prāṇas like प्राण and अपान, as also the five minor ones like नाग and कूर्म are also described.
The technique of ajapājapa of the Haṁsamantra (haṁ = I, saḥ = [am] He) is also given.
Rousing of the कुण्डलिनी power is described next.
Some of the practices expounded in हठयोग, like mudrās and bandhas, also find a place here.
The Upaniṣad ends with a description of ātmadarśana or realisation of the आत्मन्.

dhyāna
(‘[continuous] thinking.’ ‘meditation’)
------------------------------------------
A stable and concentrated मिन्द् is a great asset in life. In spiritual life, it is a must.
The art and science of concentration has been systematically described in the works on योग. The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) is the most standard treatise on this subject.
Patañjali describes eight steps to the attainment of योग, of which ध्यान happens to be the seventh or the penultimate step.
In धारणा (fixing the मिन्द् on the object of meditation), the step prior to ध्यान, the concentration is not continuous. Moments of concentration are interspersed with moments of distraction. But in ध्यान, it is continuous. Each succeeding wave of the मिन्द् is absolutely identical with the preceding wave. Say, for instance, if a person is concentrating on the form of a deity like गणपति, everyone of the mental waves carries the same impression or image of that deity. The मिन्द् is then flowing in an unbroken continuous stream like the oil that is being poured from one vessel into another.
Dhyāna practised over a long period leads to समाधि (absolute concentration resulting in mystical experience).

Dhyānayoga
(‘union [with God through] meditation’)
------------------------------------------
Dhyānayoga is the technique of meditation. The ṛṣis who could not arrive at a satisfactory or convincing answer to their queries regarding the ultimate cause of the world, are said to have taken recourse to ध्यानयोग to realise it (vide Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 1.3). In the Bhagavadgītā, the sixth chapter has been christened Dhyānayoga.
The word ‘dhyānayoga’ may mean the union (yoga = union) of the jīvātman (the individual सोउल्) with परमात्मन् (God) through ध्यान or meditation. Or, it can be interpreted as ध्यान or meditation resulting ultimately in योग or समाधि (perfect concentration) on God.
The ध्यानयोग of the Bhagavadgītā has the following steps:
The योगि should select a clean and lonely place for his practice of meditation. He should then prepare his seat by spreading the कुश grass, covering it with a deer skin and then with a cloth. He should sit on it, keeping the chest, the neck and the head erect. He must start the process of concentration by directing his sight towards the tip of his nose. He can then meditate on God, by withdrawing the मिन्द् from all other things.
The योगि should incorporate into his life the following disciplines: fearlessness, continence, faith in God, moderation in eating and sleeping, and desirelessness.
Such a योग, when practised steadily, will result in great happiness. The योगि will then be able to see all beings in himself and himself in all.
Though this योग is difficult to practise, due to the fickleness of the मिन्द्, it can be achieved by अभ्यास (repeated efforts) and वैराग्य (spirit of renunciation).
If by chance, the योगि dies before attaining its fulfilment, he will be reborn in a family with a congenial atmosphere for continuing the practice.
